content: Melvin-Koushki reports that Ibn Turka's disciple Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī, in the theoretical introduction to his Ḥulal-i Muṭarraz, posits a similar intellectual evolution: from the revelation of the Quran, whose language is the key to all knowledge, first sprang the twelve Arabic sciences; this is followed by the age of the khātam al-walāya, the Imam or Seal of Sainthood, whose potential for universal knowledge has not been actualized until the present day.
